{"translation": "In the context of `S1`, for implicit types `X` and `Y` and a given structure `N : S1 X Y` (which provides a finite type `N.A1`, a family of types `N.A3 : N.A1 → Type`, an update function `N.a5 : (n : N.A1) → ((m : N.A1) → N.A3 m) → X → N.A3 n`, together with `N.a4` and `N.a6` which are not used here), recall first the underlying relation `N.D8` on `N.A1`: for `a, b : N.A1`, `N.D8 a b` is defined as `N.D7 b a`, meaning that there exist two arbitrary global assignments `σ, σ' : (k : N.A1) → N.A3 k` (not restricted to reachable states) and an input `x : X` such that `σ k = σ' k` for all `k ≠ a`, yet `N.a5 b σ x ≠ N.a5 b σ' x` (i.e., varying the component at `a` alone can change `N.a5 b` on some input `x`). Then `Relation.TransGen N.D8 m n` means there is a finite chain `m = c_0, c_1, ..., c_k = n` in `N.A1` of length `k ≥ 1` (at least one step; zero steps do not count) with `N.D8 c_i c_{i+1}` for every `0 ≤ i < k`. The TARGET defines two propositions (`D11`, `D12`) and one natural-number-valued function (`d13`) on `N : S1 X Y` (it names them and does not assert or prove them):

1. `D11 N : Prop` holds if and only if both (a) `N.A1` is nonempty (has at least one element) and (b) for all `m, n : N.A1`, `Relation.TransGen N.D8 m n` holds—that is, from every element `m` to every element `n` there is a non-empty directed path (`k ≥ 1` steps) along `N.D8`. Because `m = n` is included and zero-step paths do not count, every element must also have a non-empty path back to itself; in particular, if `N.A1` has only one element `m`, `D11 N` requires a self-edge `N.D8 m m`.

2. `D12 N : Prop` holds if and only if for all `m, n : N.A1`, if `m ≠ n`, then it is not the case that both `Relation.TransGen N.D8 m n` and `Relation.TransGen N.D8 n m` hold. That is, no two distinct elements of `N.A1` are mutually reachable from each other via non-empty directed paths in `N.D8` (equivalently, there is no directed cycle in `N.D8` containing two or more distinct elements). Because of the hypothesis `m ≠ n`, `D12 N` does not forbid self-loops (`N.D8 m m` without visiting any other element), and it does not require `N.A1` to be nonempty.

3. `d13 N : ℕ` is defined to be `Fintype.card N.A1`, the number of elements in the finite type `N.A1` (using its `Fintype` instance `N.a2`)."}
translation:
In the context of `S1`, for implicit types `X` and `Y` and a given structure `N : S1 X Y` (which provides a finite type `N.A1`, a family of types `N.A3 : N.A1 → Type`, an update function `N.a5 : (n : N.A1) → ((m : N.A1) → N.A3 m) → X → N.A3 n`, together with `N.a4` and `N.a6` which are not used here), recall first the underlying relation `N.D8` on `N.A1`: for `a, b : N.A1`, `N.D8 a b` is defined as `N.D7 b a`, meaning that there exist two arbitrary global assignments `σ, σ' : (k : N.A1) → N.A3 k` (not restricted to reachable states) and an input `x : X` such that `σ k = σ' k` for all `k ≠ a`, yet `N.a5 b σ x ≠ N.a5 b σ' x` (i.e., varying the component at `a` alone can change `N.a5 b` on some input `x`). Then `Relation.TransGen N.D8 m n` means there is a finite chain `m = c_0, c_1, ..., c_k = n` in `N.A1` of length `k ≥ 1` (at least one step; zero steps do not count) with `N.D8 c_i c_{i+1}` for every `0 ≤ i < k`. The TARGET defines two propositions (`D11`, `D12`) and one natural-number-valued function (`d13`) on `N : S1 X Y` (it names them and does not assert or prove them):

1. `D11 N : Prop` holds if and only if both (a) `N.A1` is nonempty (has at least one element) and (b) for all `m, n : N.A1`, `Relation.TransGen N.D8 m n` holds—that is, from every element `m` to every element `n` there is a non-empty directed path (`k ≥ 1` steps) along `N.D8`. Because `m = n` is included and zero-step paths do not count, every element must also have a non-empty path back to itself; in particular, if `N.A1` has only one element `m`, `D11 N` requires a self-edge `N.D8 m m`.

2. `D12 N : Prop` holds if and only if for all `m, n : N.A1`, if `m ≠ n`, then it is not the case that both `Relation.TransGen N.D8 m n` and `Relation.TransGen N.D8 n m` hold. That is, no two distinct elements of `N.A1` are mutually reachable from each other via non-empty directed paths in `N.D8` (equivalently, there is no directed cycle in `N.D8` containing two or more distinct elements). Because of the hypothesis `m ≠ n`, `D12 N` does not forbid self-loops (`N.D8 m m` without visiting any other element), and it does not require `N.A1` to be nonempty.

3. `d13 N : ℕ` is defined to be `Fintype.card N.A1`, the number of elements in the finite type `N.A1` (using its `Fintype` instance `N.a2`).

divergences.description: D12 omits the essential requirement in [P-HW] that Hanson and Walker's strictly feed-forward architecture realize a deterministic finite-state automaton using 'simple elementary components' (specifically flip-flops). D12 enforces only the causal-graph ordering condition (no directed cycles of length >= 2 among units in N.A1, which on finite N.A1 is equivalent to a linear ordering in which no unit depends on a strictly later one while self-loops are allowed), while leaving each unit's state type N.A3 n : Type and self-update rule N.a5 n completely unconstrained (not restricted to flip-flops, elementary components, or even finite types). As a result, any arbitrarily complex or recurrent network N : S1 X Y can be trivially repackaged into a single-unit network (A1 = Unit, A3 () = N.D1) that vacuously satisfies D12 with identical input-output behavior, trivializing the Krohn-Rhodes strictly feed-forward architecture described in [P-HW].

Because D11 requires only Nonempty N.A1 (at least one unit) rather than at least two units, any single-unit system with a self-loop (such as a single flip-flop, e.g., d15 in the context) satisfies both D11 and D12 simultaneously. Although D11 literally matches claim (i)'s wording ('there is at least one unit, and every unit lies on feedback loops with every unit'), this overlap on 1-unit self-looping systems is in tension with [P-D52b] (where conscious recurrent systems with phi > 0 and feedforward systems with phi = 0 are mutually exclusive) and [P-HW] (where strictly feed-forward flip-flop architectures have Phi = 0 for all states).

Neither D11 nor D12 formalizes IIT's quantitative integrated-information measure (phi > 0, 'arbitrarily high phi' in [P-D52b], or 'Phi = 0 for all states' in [P-HW]); D11 also requires strong connectivity across all units of the whole system rather than just recurrence with phi > 0. Because claim (i) explicitly describes D11 as a structural stand-in and disclaims equivalence to phi > 0, this is a minor, disclosed idealization.

While d13 N := Fintype.card N.A1 faithfully counts the number of units in N as stated in claim (iii), the unconstrained per-unit state types N.A3 n : Type in S1 mean that d13 counts abstract components whose individual state capacity is unbounded, rather than bounded elementary 'neurons' as in [P-D54].

judgement.summary: D11 and d13 match claims (i) and (iii) as structural definitions (with minor caveats around the absence of phi, unbounded per-unit state spaces, and D11 overlapping D12 on 1-unit self-loops such as a single flip-flop). However, D12 has a major divergence from [P-HW]: by checking only acyclicity between distinct units without restricting components to simple elementary components (flip-flops) or even finite-state machines, it allows any arbitrary system to trivially satisfy D12 by collapsing all state into a single unit.
